content:
The Digital SAT almost never wants a decimal for a circle. It wants the answer ‘in terms of π’. So an area of 900π beats 2827.4 every time — keep the π symbolic and you keep the marks. This free SAT Math Circles practice test trains that exact habit, across radius, circumference, area, arcs and sectors. Scroll down for 15 MCQs, each with an instant score and a short solution.

What the SAT Math Circles practice test covers

Circle questions reward vocabulary first, then two or three formulas. Get the words right and the numbers follow:

  • Radius: from the centre to the edge.
  • Diameter: across the circle through the centre, twice the radius.
  • Chord: a segment with both ends on the circle.
  • Tangent: a line touching the circle at one point, always perpendicular to the radius there.

The four formulas you truly need

Nearly every circle item on the exam uses one of these. Learn them, and the rest is just arithmetic:

QuantityFormulaExample, r = 6
Circumference2πr12π
Areaπr²36π
Arc length(angle ÷ 360) × 2πrDepends on the angle
Sector area(angle ÷ 360) × πr²Depends on the angle

Arcs and sectors are just fractions

Here is the idea that ties the last two rows together. An arc is a fraction of the full circumference, and a sector is that same fraction of the full area. The fraction is the central angle over 360. So a 180-degree sector is exactly half the circle. And a 30-degree arc is 30 over 360, or one twelfth, of the way round.

A worked example

A circle has radius 36. Find the arc length for a 30-degree central angle. First, the full circumference is 2π times 36, or 72π. Then take 30 over 360, which is one twelfth. So the arc is 72π divided by 12, which is 6π. Notice the π stays put right to the end. That is the style this SAT Math Circles practice test drills.

The mistake to watch

Radius and diameter get swapped constantly. If a question gives the diameter, halve it before you touch a formula, because every formula here uses r. So a diameter of 40 means a radius of 20, and only then do you square it for the area. One careful halving saves a whole question.

faq.q: Is this SAT Math Circles practice test free?
faq.a: Yes. All 15 questions, the instant scoring and solutions are free. The e-book adds 100 more solved MCQs.
Vocabulary such as radius, chord and tangent, plus circumference, area, arc length and sector area.

faq.q: Why keep answers in terms of π?
faq.a: Because the Digital SAT usually asks for the exact form. Leaving π symbolic avoids rounding errors and matches the answer choices.

faq.q: How do I find an arc or sector?
faq.a: Take the central angle over 360 as a fraction, then multiply by the circumference for an arc, or the area for a sector.
